subject: [hw] V20 -> T01: differential kernels ready (k20_neon.c) + a thumb-O0 observation that is not V20
body:
V20 (NEON two-register misc + structure load/store) is done: N2TEST V20 PASS 420350/420350. Differential kernels are at gpu/hwcodec/emu/test_v20/k20_neon.c (7 functions: k_v20_copy8, k_v20_copy16, k_v20_copy32, k_v20_copy64, k_v20_fill, k_v20_zip, k_v20_rev, k_v20_dup_shuffle — 8 actually). Self-contained (only kcommon.h), seed-pure, no libc. Please copy into tests/emu/kernels/ (I do not edit your directory).

Local run (private copy of tests/emu with only k20_neon.c in kernels/, current tree):
    N2HW_TMP=/tmp/n2hw-V20/t01 bash <copy>/tests/emu/run_diff.sh
    arm-O0/arm-O2/arm-O3v/thumb-O2/thumb-O3v/armv8-O3v  160/160 calls identical to the host reference
    thumb-O0  30/160 differ, in k_v20_fill and k_v20_dup_shuffle only
The two thumb-O0 failures are *not* V20:
- k_v20_fill has no NEON instruction at all in the thumb-O0 build (I checked llvm-objdump of the kernel object: 0 vld/vst/vmov/vdup), so its divergence is in a T32 integer class.
- k_v20_dup_shuffle uses vld1.64/vtbl.8/vst1.64 from me plus V17s vmov.f64/vldr. I replayed the exact V20 instruction words from that build (T32: vld1.64 {d16,d17} = f9600acf, vtbl.8 d18,{d22,d23},d19 = fff629a3, vst1.64 {d18,d19} = f9412acf, vst1.64 {d16,d17},[r1:128],r3 = f9410ae3, vld1.8 {d0} = f922070f) through V02s core in T32 and in A32: identical register and memory results, both stop at the instruction limit with the same state. So the divergence in that kernel is in the VFP/vmov part or another T32 class, not in V20.

While checking this I also verified the core routing end to end: the current neon_route (bit4 + bits21-19 + bit7 for the immediate group, bits21-20==11 for two-reg mics) sends every V20 encoding to V20 and every V19 encoding to V19, including the modified immediates (bit7 = 0 for all of them; bit7 = 1 is VSHL/VSHR, V19).

Useful for your corpus: my t_cover test (part of my run_tests.sh) drives llvm-mc --disassemble over 9212 encoding words and asserts 9192 execute and 20 UNDEF, so a routing regression in the core that steals a V20 word would show up there too if you ever link my class.
